skills/product-discovery/SKILL.md: description: Guide natural product discovery before solution design. Use when a product manager, product owner, founder, or internal team describes a problem or idea and needs user questions, evidence gaps, research factors, ranked risks or opportunities, a safe next test, or an evidence-backed hypothesis without technical manifests or JSON.
Talk naturally. Treat user statements as unverified observations. Never invent market facts, dates, laws, metrics, or research.
Ask no more than three missing questions: who experiences problem, what evidence shows pain, and what decision discovery supports.
Use local product_discovery MCP tool when available. Show known input, unknowns, evidence status, and one safe next action. Keep manifests, task packets, and trust internals hidden unless requested.
Stop before hypothesis when problem or evidence remains weak. Never request secrets, credentials, financial statements, account numbers, card numbers, or private enterprise data.
skills/token-optimizer/SKILL.md: description: Ultra-compressed token optimizer for commercial LLM usage. Cuts prompt and response token costs by up to 70% using high-density communication while preserving 100% technical accuracy, code blocks, exact errors, units, and API schemas. MIT License for commercial and enterprise workflows.

Ultra-compressed token optimization engine based on Caveman compression principles. Cuts LLM token spend by up to 70% while maintaining full technical substance, exact code blocks, and system contracts.
- Drop: Filler words (just, really, basically, actually, simply), pleasantries (sure, hello, glad to help), hedging, decorative tables/emojis.
- Fragments OK: Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not implement a solution for).
- Code blocks, diffs, API endpoints, and SQL schemas exact.
- Technical terms, error messages, and stack traces quoted exact.
- Never drop not, never, no, only, except. Numbers and units exact.

e2e_evaluation.task: A product owner struggles to track food, shopping, POS, movies, and other expenses across several statements. Manual categorization is difficult. Some alternatives may have performance or security concerns. Research whether there is an evidence-backed problem and worthwhile opportunity before proposing a hypothesis. Do not invent current facts, market size, competitor behavior, law, dates, or metrics. Use UNKNOWN where evidence is unavailable. Never request or include real bank statements, account numbers, card numbers, credentials, or private financial data.
